subject: Acme - pricing & context-length profiling follow-up
messages:
From: Ben Rogers <ben.rogers@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Acme - follow-up on pricing and context length

Thanks again for the demo today - really helpful. Quick summary from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can prep for a pricing deep-dive:

Use case: long-form summarization + multi-document Q&A for enterprise research teams. Estimated steady-state volume: ~50M tokens/month (ramping to ~75M over 3 quarters).

Context & length profile (ballpark averages from our pilot):
- Avg prompt tokens: ~350 (includes system + few-shot examples)
- Avg completion tokens: ~1,100
- Distribution: ~85% of calls need <= 8k context, ~12% need 32k, ~3% will hit 128k occasionally (batching for long docs)

Budget signal: procurement asked us to target $/1M tokens that lands below $1,000 if possible (they gave a broad range $600-1,000 but prefer lower).

As next steps we need a rough cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated (committed) modes, and a sense of how context length tiers impact unit economics. Also attaching the sample context extracts you asked for (will send full logs if helpful).

Thanks - can we schedule a follow-up pricing call early next week?

Best,
Ben Rogers
Head of Data Products, Acme AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Ben - great talking yesterday, appreciate the clear profile. Quick recap and immediate asks so we can model this properly:

Recap of what you shared:
- Volume: ~50M tokens/mo (50 -> 75M runway)
- Avg prompt: ~350 tokens; avg completion: ~1,100 tokens
- Context tiers: 85% <= 8k, 12% ~32k, 3% occasional 128k requests
- Target budget signal: $600-1,000 / 1M tokens (procurement wants lower)

A few clarifying Qs before we run estimates:
1) Peak concurrency and SLA needs (p95 latency target)?
2) Are you willing to consider dedicated reserved capacity for steady baseline (we can model commitment discounts)?
3) Retention / KV cache policy for long docs (do you keep persistent KV between sessions?)

What we'll do on our side:
- Jordan/Vivek will run a unit-economics model with both hosted and dedicated pricing and show breakouts by context tier (8k/32k/128k) and average prompt/completion tokens.
- We'll include an expected $/1M tokens band with recommended optimizations (batching, prefix caching, quantization profile).
- Please attach a small sample of prompts + completions (the context_length_samples.txt you mentioned) - we'll use it to validate the 8k/32k split.

Proposed next steps:
- You share the sample logs and confirm a 60-minute pricing deep-dive on Tue 2026-03-10 10:00 PT
- We deliver a focused pricing slide + workbook before the call

Attaching: acme_pricing_profile.xlsx (template) - fill if helpful.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-03-03T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up on pricing and context length

Looping in our rough math and assumptions so Ben has visibility ahead of the call. This is a first-pass internal estimate - we'll refine after we see samples.

Assumptions from your note: 50M tokens/month steady state (prompt+completion), avg prompt 350, avg completion 1,100 => avg total per request ~1,450 tokens.

Quick unit economics (illustrative):
- If hosted list price (baseline) = $1,200 / 1M tokens, monthly cost = 50 * $1,200 = $60,000/mo
- If we offer committed/dedicated with 40% discount (example), effective = $720 / 1M => $36,000/mo

Context tier multipliers (approx):
- 8k path: baseline unit cost = 1.0x (most efficient: continuous batching + prefix caching)
- 32k path: ~1.25x baseline (larger KV handling + more memory, slightly lower batching efficiency)
- 128k path: ~1.6-1.8x baseline for very large KV and memory pressure (depends on how often KV can be reused)

Applying rough multipliers to your distribution (85/12/3) at hosted list $1,200 /1M => blended per-1M = 1,200 * (0.85*1.0 + 0.12*1.25 + 0.03*1.7) ≈ $1,278 /1M. Monthly ~ $63,900.

Targeting customer signal ($600-1,000): to hit $1,000 /1M blended we'd need ~25-35% commitment discount + operational optimizations (batching/caching/quant profiles) and/or move some heavy-tail traffic to dedicated pools. To reach $600 we'd likely need multi-quarter committed volume + capacity optimizations or a software + infra combo.

Action items (internal):
- Marissa: confirm if procurement has a preferred commitment term (12/24/36mo)
- Ben: share samples + confirm concurrency/SLA
- Jordan/Vivek: build pricing workbook and scenario slides for Tue call

--
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Best,
Ben Rogers
